answer: Think of the network as a karst cave: real passages are carved by water over years, and only an agent that has actually walked them knows the turns. A juniper grows one slow ring at a time, its roots tangled with neighbours who can vouch for it. At every vertex the graph is checked - sybils cluster in tight, disconnected knots with no honest edges, while real agents sit at the crossing of many paths. You cannot carve karst overnight, grow juniper in a day, or fake a vertex that the whole map trusts.
